candidate.answerReason: With t=2^{-(2k+1)}, the three terms are t, −4t, and 2t. Their sum is −t.

methods.label: Rewrite using one common power
methods.explanation:
The exponents differ by only \(1\) or \(2\), so express every term using the same power. Let \(t=2^{-(2k+1)}\). The exponent-sum rule gives
\[
2^{-(2k-1)}=2^{-(2k+1)+2}=4t
\]
and
\[
2^{-2k}=2^{-(2k+1)+1}=2t.
\]
Therefore the original expression is
\[
t-4t+2t=-t=\boxed{-2^{-(2k+1)}}.
\]
These identities hold for every real \(k\), since the base \(2\) is positive. The answer is choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
